name: JANUS INTERNATIONAL GROUP

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am still anchoring on a trough that is actually a new normal. Self-storage was over-built in the 2021-23 boom; REIT street rates have been negative for three years; and Janus's own management, in the one document where it must be honest about the future, assumed enough deterioration to write off Kiwi II goodwill inside twelve months and to leave the core business 18% from impairment. The TTM free cash flow conversion of 203% that makes the cash look real is itself the tell: capex HALVED from $26.0M to $13.7M, and a conversion ratio that RISES while EBITDA falls 22.7% is working capital and underinvestment, not earning power. On an FY2027 EBITDA of $100M the FCFF base is roughly $74M, at which the market's requirement is only -3.0% and the fair value is $1.82-$3.29 - at or below today's price.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: FY2027 guidance at the Q4 print, and specifically whether adjusted EBITDA is guided above or below $120M; plus Public Storage, Extra Space and CubeSmart 2027 development capital plans, and whether R3 stops declining.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Most of it. R3 -10.6% refutes the counter-cyclical offset; organic revenue is down ~9%; the Kiwi II goodwill write-down is in the filing; and the Janus Core 18% headroom disclosure is management telling you its own forecast moved down.
devils_advocate.unresolved: FY2027 EBITDA, which is the whole answer and on which the company has given no guidance. The fair-value range across defensible bases and discount rates is $1.82 to $13.14 against a $3.75 price, and the sign flips on an input nobody has published.

what_changed: Q3 2026 (10-Q and release, 2026-11-10; stock -28.6% on the day). Revenue $213.1M -2.8%; 9M revenue $669.3M +1.7% but ENTIRELY acquired. Adjusted EBITDA Q3 $34.0M -22.0%, 9M $107.2M -18.2%. FY guidance cut again: adjusted EBITDA to $127-133M from the ~$160M midpoint the 2026-09-16 pass used. $18.3M of non-cash impairments, of which $7.4M is GOODWILL AT KIWI II - an acquisition closed inside 2026 and written down in its first year - plus $5.0M at BETCO and $5.9M on the DBCI and ACT tradenames, with ACT written to zero. The same note discloses that Janus Core's reporting unit fair value exceeds carrying value by only 18.0% ($257.3M) and the Janus Core tradename by only 12.3% ($66.8M): management's own DCF puts the CORE business within 12-18% of further impairment. Offsetting: a $30.0M voluntary term-loan prepayment in Q3, no revolver drawn, term loan repriced 50bp tighter in February 2026 to SOFR+200, rate 5.75% at 2026-10-03, maturity 2030. 9M operating cash flow $94.6M, free cash flow $86.5M; TTM FCF $105.7M against TTM adjusted net income $52.0M, a 203% conversion.
consensus_case: Janus sells doors, hallway systems and smart-entry hardware into self-storage new construction and retrofit. Its end market is set by rates and by the REIT development pipelines, and both are shut. FY2026 guidance now reads revenue $855-865M (-2.7%) with adjusted EBITDA $127-133M, DOWN 22.7%, and margin 16.0% against 19.9% a year earlier. Q3 revenue fell 2.8% to $213.1M even WITH $10.7M of acquired Kiwi II revenue in it; stripping the $55-60M of guided inorganic revenue leaves organic revenue down roughly 9%. Both legs are falling at once: Self-Storage -5.0% (New Construction -1.6% including the acquisition, R3 retrofit -10.6%) with only Commercial +2.3%. Q3 carried $18.3M of impairments and an operating LOSS of $5.5M. At 7.2x guided EBITDA on 52% debt weight with net leverage already 2.9x and rising as EBITDA falls, the market is pricing a levered equity stub in a market with no visible floor and no 2027 guidance. That is a coherent price, not a panic.
base_case_rationale: I do not underwrite recovery and I do not underwrite collapse. Self-storage new construction is deferred rather than destroyed - the facilities get built when rates allow - but nothing in this quarter says when, and the prior pass's structural hedge has been refuted: R3 retrofit, which is supposed to be counter-cyclical because it monetises existing facilities, fell 10.6%, worse than New Construction. Both legs declining together removes the offset the 2026-09-16 thesis leaned on. Against that, the business still converts: 9M FCF of $86.5M in a bad year, capex of only $8.1M against $10.8M of PP&E depreciation and $49.9M of total D&A (most of which is purchase-accounting amortisation, not a cash cost), no revolver drawn and $30M of debt voluntarily repaid. I assume margins hold near 16% and revenue stops falling but does not recover, giving FCFF drifting down about 3% a year.
key_risks: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is unguided and the 2026 rate of decline was -22.7%; one repeat takes net leverage past 3.8x
Janus Core reporting unit fair value exceeds carrying value by only 18.0% and its tradename by 12.3% - management's own DCF is close to a further write-down
Kiwi II goodwill impaired $7.4M within a year of purchase; the acquired revenue is dilutive to mix (the EFOR pattern)
Capex halved to $13.7M TTM against $10.8M of 9M PP&E depreciation - reported free cash flow is flattered by underinvestment
Equity is 55% of enterprise value, so a 20% error in EV is a 36% error in the equity
watch_for: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance at the Q4 print - above or below $120M decides this name
Whether R3 retrofit revenue stops declining; it is the leg that is supposed to be counter-cyclical and it is falling fastest
A further impairment at the Janus Core reporting unit, which management has already flagged at 18% headroom
